title: Political writing: getting beyond the self
summary: From individual experience to shared problems.
body:
Course themes

  • The rise of the first person
  • Autofiction, autoethnography and the limits of testimony
  • Authorship and political legitimacy
  • Political essay, cultural criticism and the manifesto
  • Formal experimentation and collective writing

What will we work on?

Writing short texts that frame shared problems and open up spaces for political discussion.

Context and approach

Autofiction, the personal essay and first-person narratives hold a central place in contemporary culture. The course discusses their political and aesthetic possibilities and limits, and asks what is left out of the story when biography becomes the main source of legitimacy.

We will read essays, manifestos, cultural criticism and experimental forms of writing. Discussion will be combined with exercises aimed at producing short texts of public intervention, paying attention to the relations between experience and structure, authorship and collective thought.
introduction: How do we move from personal experience to an analysis of the collective conditions that produce it? A space for reading and writing to build arguments, intervene in conflicts and experiment with other ways of saying things.
